text: is a Python-based GIS library used to explore, manipulate, and manage the railway data. Using Geopandas, it is simple to convert from the original “4326” coordinate reference system (CRS) that uses units of degrees for lat/long to the “3857” CRS that maps those points to meters. The source line data is used to determine “optimal” routes from origin/destination pairs is determined by manual inspection of nodes to represent railway yards. The A* algorithm provided by the NetworkX Python library is used for this. The weights between nodes are set to be the line segment distance between the nodes. This results in selecting the minimum distance routes with the constraint of railroad ownership or track rights and the mainline or yard track type. Further processing of the location data used to refine the line segments between nodes. The locations used to define the route are more uniformly distributed along the route while maintaining the “to” and “from” nodes from the NARN database. In some cases this removes excess locations that are close to each other and in other cases adds additional locations to not exceed a maximum distance (200 meters) between locations. Once this is completed, an elevation database (originally we used a service provided by USGS, but later chose to use the elevation service provided by Google§§ since it was more robust and faster) is queried for the elevations given the lat/long coordinates. With the elevations for the locations, the gradients can be determined. In some cases, it was necessary to smooth out the elevations with a filter to better satisfy the known constraint that nearly all Class 1 freight railways do not exceed a 2.2% grade. Small variation in elevations that occur over short distances get averaged out with the length of most consists. The import element of elevation are long grades, their steepness, and total elevation changes. After the elevations have been smoothed the curvatures for line segments between two nodes is calculated using Menger curvature. The algorithm starts by taking three contiguous points and determining the angle of curvature for a 100 foot arc that includes them. This is not exactly correct but does provide close approximation to distribute actual curvature (and thus a source of drag) along the route. This curvature is also used to establish maximum speed for the segment based on accepted rules by the railroad industry. No corrections or modifications are included for super elevation, the banking of curves to reduce roll-over hazards for curves. B.
